context: Real-time streaming line chart of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, rendering at 10 values/sec via canvas with a 60-second scrolling main view and a 5-minute LTTB-downsampled overview navigator with brush selection; stats bar shows current/min/max/mean/std/point count.
first_impression: Exceptionally clean for a live-streaming chart — one series, one color, two clearly hierarchical views, and a compact stats bar that adds context without clutter.
what_works: Single blue series with gradient fill keeps color load at minimum (1 hue); main chart → overview layout creates an obvious focus/context hierarchy that guides the eye naturally without requiring explanation.
what_doesnt: At screenshot time (only 40 points, ~4 seconds elapsed) the overview and main chart span identical time ranges, making the navigator redundant and its brushable purpose unclear until more data accumulates; continuous rAF animation cannot be perceptually assessed from a static screenshot, so smoothness and object constancy during fast scrolling remain unverified.
